agent_answer_excerpt:
Active customers are a governed defined class (kp:ActiveCustomer): a customer with at least one order in the last 2 years. I resolve the count through its bound membership flag (customer_order_in_context.is_active_customer) rather than writing the 2-year rule by hand, so the figure matches the governed definition. The "last 2 years" window is anchored to the data's max order date (2024-04-20), not today — i.e. orders from 2022-04-20 onward. The query returns the distinct count of customers flagged active; that number is the answer.

Basis: kp:ActiveCustomer (governed defined class, bound measure) | Freshness: 2024-04-20 (2-year window anchored to max_date, not today) | Steward: steward of kp:ActiveCustomer (sales)

agent_answer_excerpt: No — customer lifetime value (CLV/LTV) is not a governed metric in the Knowledge Plane. It does not appear in the routing table, and absence from the table is conclusive: every governed concept is listed there, so there is no governed CLV definition or binding to resolve to. The closest governed things are customer-level building blocks (kp:Customer, kp:TotalSales, kp:OrderCount, kp:AverageOrderValue, kp:ActiveCustomer) — an LTV figure could be improvised from those, but it would be ungoverned / exploratory, not official, so I'd label it as such if you want one.
